facts.fact: The case study says Botswana's health sector comprises numerous digital health systems that operate in isolation, constraining interoperability and limiting data exchange; dated by publication, no event date given.

note: The architecture (developed 2023-2024, with a Master Patient Index and Shared Health Record) is a blueprint with no exchange stated as built or in service, so no underway fact.

facts.fact: The estimates record P28,934,000 appropriated for MoH Computerisation, and its notes cite the Committee of Supply speech describing a Health Information Exchange and a Client Registry keyed on the Omang or passport number as ready for deployment; dated by the fiscal-year start, 2026/27.

The Minister of Local Government told Parliament that the Patient Information Management System, Integrated Patient Management System, DHIS2 and E Pulse are active but not interfaced to permit data sharing across all health facilities.

The minister said an Electronic Medical Records system is being piloted in two districts and, with the Clinic Information Management System, will link to the Botswana Health Information Exchange supporting a Master Patient Index across public and private facilities.

The Ministry of Health's Committee of Supply speech reports the Health Information Exchange being implemented, with its Client Registry and Facilities Registry ready for deployment and further expansion planned next financial year.

note: The document states nothing on this study's aspects for this country that the study's questions ask.
US PEPFAR/donor funding for interoperable health information systems stated only as an aim; no exchange contracted, piloted or in service for the country.

facts.fact: The World Bank approved on 26 January 2026 US$13.1 million of IBRD financing under Botswana's HEPRR project to enhance the health information exchange (HIE) by linking digital systems including the EMR and eIDSR, and by developing and linking registries.
